description: Story 21.7 — « Portail client » (module client-portal, free), aligned on Bref's « retrouver mes factures » on 11/11/2026: an end client of the merchants (never a Keevo user) creates his account once with a code sent to his phone, a name and a password (optional e-mail), then signs in by phone or e-mail + password without SMS (Bref's flow); signing in with a code alone stays possible (it is also the way back after a forgotten password: register again with a new code). He lists the invoices every merchant issued to that phone, each with what Bref's screens show (lines, payments, paid / remaining, merchant phone) and a link to the PDF. Public paths (no merchant JWT): the portal has its own session token 'kvc_…' (24 hours, like Bref's client token), sent as 'Authorization: Bearer kvc_…' on GET /api/v1/portal/invoices only. A merchant JWT is refused there (401 PORTAL_SESSION_INVALID) and the portal token is refused everywhere else. Like Bref, the portal is on for every company; the merchant can still switch it off: module client-portal in « Mes modules » (PUT /api/v1/tenants/me/modules/client-portal/activation) — off = its invoices disappear from the portal at the next request. Responses use Keevo's envelope: success {data, …}; error {error: French message to show, code: HTTP name, domainCode, details?}. No identifier is ever returned: show the fields as they are. Change this file only with both sides; fields are only ever added.

headers.Accept-Language: optional, fr (default) or en — language of the SMS

errors.reaction: show the message, keep the form
not a phone (an email is refused): « Saisissez un numéro de téléphone »
phone missing or too long: show the message
show the message, disable « Renvoyer le code » for a few minutes

endpoints.notes: Bref's POST /v1/clients/otp/request. Same answer whether the phone has invoices or not. The code goes by SMS (and WhatsApp when configured), 6 digits, valid 5 minutes; it is used by /register (Bref's flow) or /otp/verify. Limits shared with the merchant sign-in codes of the same phone: 3 per 10 minutes, 5 per hour, 10 per hour per network address.

request.name: Awa Ndiaye (1–120 characters)
request.phone: same value as the code request

errors.reaction: « Code incorrect ou expiré » — let the client retype or ask a new code
the code is dead: ask a new one
show the message, retry later
too many attempts for this phone or address: show the message, retry in a few minutes
show the message on the e-mail field; the code is used: ask a new one and send another e-mail or none (told only after a valid code, so nobody can probe e-mails)
show the message, back to the phone screen
not a phone, malformed e-mail or password over 72 bytes: show the message
field missing, password under 8 characters: show the message

endpoints.notes: Bref's POST /v1/clients/register (name, phone, password, otpCode → here 'code', email?). Bref's minimum password length is 6: Keevo asks 8 (same rule as merchant accounts). Bref refused a phone that already had an account (422); here the code proves the phone, so registering again sets the new password (and the e-mail when sent) and signs out the other devices — the « mot de passe oublié » path. Bref's refreshToken is not returned (Bref had no refresh route for clients): sign in again after 24 h.

errors.reaction: « Numéro, e-mail ou mot de passe incorrect. » — same answer for an unknown client, an account without password and a wrong password; offer « Recevoir un code » (register again)
show the message, retry in a few minutes
field missing: show the message

endpoints.notes: Bref's POST /v1/clients/login: no code, no SMS. Failed sign-ins never block registering again with a new code (separate limit). Limits (Bref's 'login'): 30 attempts per address and 10 per phone / e-mail per 15 minutes, right or wrong.

errors.reaction: « Code incorrect ou expiré » — let the client retype or ask a new code
the code is dead: ask a new one
show the message, retry later
show the message, back to the phone screen
not a phone: back to the phone screen
phone or code missing: show the message
rare: the code may already be used — offer « Recevoir un nouveau code »

endpoints.notes: Sign-in with the code alone (no account needed, no password). Store accessToken in the secure store (never in plain storage, never logged). A merchant sign-in code is refused here and a portal code is refused on /api/v1/auth/otp/verify.

items.paymentState: UNPAID | PARTIAL | PAID | OVERDUE | CANCELLED (colour only, never shown)
items.paymentStateLabel: Non payée | Partiellement payée | Payée | En retard | Annulée

errors.reaction: delete the stored token, back to the sign-in screen
show the message, retry after a minute
bad cursor or limit: reload from the first page

endpoints.notes: Bref's GET /v1/clients/invoices, paged: newest first across merchants, limit 1–50 (20 by default). Keep paging while nextCursor is not null: a page may hold fewer items than the limit (an invoice no longer listable is skipped), even none, without being the last one. 'summary' (Bref's header: number of invoices, amount) is on the first page only (null / absent on the next ones): invoiceCount counts every listed invoice; totalTtc is the sum of their printed totals (totalTtc), leaving out the cancelled ones (credit notes and payments are not subtracted: they show per invoice in amountRemaining). Exact, never truncated. The detail screen reads the item itself (Bref read its cache): lines (unitPrice as typed — excluding VAT when the invoice's prices exclude it; totalTtc with VAT), payments (received: paid + paidDate; instalments: dueDate, paid false until settled), amountPaid, amountRemaining (0 when cancelled), merchantPhone. 'link' is null for a cancelled invoice. The link opens the invoice PDF without sign-in and stops after 24 h: never cache it, re-list to get a fresh one. Amounts are XAF integers. Online only (no offline copy). Not ported from Bref: GET /v1/invoices/public/count (it told anyone whether a phone has invoices) — go straight to sign-in.

endpoints.response: 204, no body (also when the token is unknown)
endpoints.notes: Delete the stored token whatever the answer. Too many unknown tokens from one address are ignored (still 204).
